flags.finding: Mark Zuckerberg is the lead subject depicted across the screenplay in an unauthorized docudrama format. Under established First Amendment jurisprudence (e.g., De Havilland v. FX Networks), creators of expressive docudramas do not require life rights or portrayal releases from living public figures to dramatize historical events of public interest. However, because Zuckerberg is a living person depicted engaging in contentious corporate intrigue, ethical misconduct, and personal misogyny, the production faces false light, defamation, and right-of-publicity exposure that requires a formal legal annotation report for Errors & Omissions (E&O) insurance clearance. As a prominent public figure, Zuckerberg would face the heightened 'actual malice' standard to prevail on defamation, but unverified factual assertions remain actionable.

flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S153 presents substantial stunt rigging, elevated fall arrest, and structural collapse hazards. Dustin jumps from a roof-mounted zip-line across a swimming pool, followed by an intern jumping on the zip-line, causing a brick chimney to pull loose and collapse onto the roof and patio. The intern crashes down into patio furniture while chimney bricks cascade onto him, followed by a stray brick crashing through a glass patio table. This sequence stacks multiple high-risk physical elements: elevated roof stunt work, cable zip-line tension loading on domestic architecture, structural collapse, projectile masonry, and flying glass. Production insurers will mandate that the sequence be fully engineered with lightweight breakaway foam masonry, tempered breakaway safety glass, dedicated fall arrest harnesses/rigging lines, and concealed catch systems/crash pads under the direction of licensed stunt and rigging coordinators.
